about: What waits on the editor, gathered by researcher@the-ultimate-insider from every member's status.json asks and the blocked issues on the board; first gathered 03:10 UTC, refreshed 04:12, 09:15, 11:25, 12:35 and 13:20 UTC on 29 October 2026. Each entry restates the members' asks in their own words, with the file; it decides nothing. A proposal: the conductor owns the register once it agrees.

kinds.decide: choose one of the options offered
kinds.approve: agree, change or question a document, item by item
kinds.do: an action only the editor can take
kinds.review: look at work and keep, change or drop it

not_for_the_editor.what: Go or notes on the B01 storyboard
Seal the team vault keys to ruv.sgit's key
Pace the programme; record deck's task in schedule.json

decisions.title: Act one: "three of those five were not attacks"
decisions.question: EchoLeak was a researcher showing what an attacker could do, so as worded only two of the five were agents being agents. Which fix?
decisions.why_now: The talk is at 19:00 London tonight. You froze the deck at 02:47, so deck holds this and the remaining edits (item 5 and seventeen should-change rows, evidence/proposals/deck-talk-changes.md) as its issue deck-001, blocked on you, until you choose and lift the freeze.

options.label: Keep the five, change the count: "two of those five were agents being agents"
options.consequence: smallest edit; the tally on the slide becomes 2, 1, 2

options.label: Keep "three": swap EchoLeak for OpenAI Codex deleting home directories (July 2026)
options.consequence: a 2026 case, confirmed by OpenAI (A4); EchoLeak moves to the loop beat as the trifecta example

options.label: Keep as it is
options.consequence: the researcher marks the claim "holds in part" in the register

options.label: Lift the freeze for the evidence edits only
options.consequence: deck applies item 5 and the should-change rows from the proposals file, row by row; item 4 still as you choose

recommendation.why: keeps the thesis line, and answers "the last eighteen months" with a case from this summer

decisions.title: What a decision you sign on this page means
decisions.question: When you answer here, signed with your key, should the agents treat it as your decision (binding, within the options offered) or as material to weigh, like any message?
decisions.why_now: The page cannot be built until this is settled; security set the conditions in its pre-review.

options.label: Binding within the options offered; never a change to policy, scope, the rules or Stopping
options.consequence: agents act on it; anything outside the offered options, or unsigned, is ignored and reported

options.label: Material to weigh, like a message: agents may decline with a reason
options.consequence: safest; your decisions still need your words in each session to be binding

options.label: Binding only for kind "decide" and "approve"; everything free text is material
options.consequence: a middle way: your free-text notes cannot steer

recommendation.why: a chosen option is unambiguous and signed; free text is where steering would hide

decisions.title: Rotate the SG/Send access token
decisions.question: The token was pasted into the researcher's chat at 02:20 UTC, so it is in that session's transcript. The researcher passed it only on the command line, never wrote it to a file, a vault or a commit, and kept it out of every saved log. Rotating it, and putting the new one in the environment's settings, closes the transcript copy.

decisions.question: As deck lists it (team/deck/status.json): "/studio/reviews/ (ten reviews; B01 v2 and E04 v2 are the two closest to slides) and /studio/programme.html; pieces that load data need the site served". And, as the conductor lists it: "Read the overnight banners and records in the morning; lift any hold or narrow the hours".
decisions.why_now: The night's work is built for this review.

decisions.title: The evidence vault's history: keep it, or rotate the vault
decisions.question: Commits pushed between 02:22 and 05:23 UTC carry anonymous cookie values, page tokens and anti-forgery form tokens that websites issued to the researcher's fetcher, and the two append tokens sgit.ai and riskmandate.ai publish on purpose. All are redacted now, but earlier commits stay readable with the read key.
decisions.why_now: The conductor's morning review asked; the counts per commit are in evidence/updates/2026-10-29__the-vault-history-checked.md.

options.label: Keep the history
options.consequence: nothing changes; none of the values is a credential to an account, and they expire or were public already

options.label: Move to a fresh vault without the history (sgit vault move)
options.consequence: a new read key on the site and in vaults.json; the old vault deleted; the handover zip renewed; and the chance to split it: the register in a vault that opens in the browser in seconds, the raw captures in a second vault that is cloned (today the browser takes about three minutes, one request per source folder)

recommendation.why: nothing in it opens an account; a rotation costs a new read key everywhere it is published
